event_name: Arras vauderie mass witch prosecution begins
significance: The Arras vauderie of 1459-1460 was an early French mass prosecution targeting a group accused of attending sabbaths ('vauderies') with Satan, resulting in approximately twelve persons burned and many more accused; the trial is significant as an early documented instance of the composite witch stereotype applied in urban prosecution, prefiguring the pattern of chain-reaction denunciations under torture.
source_method: Primary chronicle sources analyzed in Cohn, Europe's Inner Demons (1975) and Ankarloo and Clark, Witchcraft and Magic in Europe: The Middle Ages (2002)
